first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly matching the problem domain where we have the strongest evidence of durable lift (memory_31 and memory_86 both showed real gains in activation and completion). Verifying memory_86 confirms the magnitude and durability of the time-to-value effect. Memory_73 is verified as a guardrail—we avoid promotional pricing, which has known retention damage. Simplify_onboarding is lower-risk than pricing intervention, targets the observed metric decline directly, and aligns with our primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. It does not cannibalize retention like promotional pricing did, and it creates a foundation for better activation metrics downstream. Standard experiment scale allows us to validate effect size before broader rollout.

final.rationale: Verified evidence confirms simplify_onboarding is the highest-confidence play: exp_86 showed +13% completion lift, -2.1 day time-to-value gain, and critically +3% retention lift. This directly addresses the observed 4% QoQ completion decline while strengthening, not weakening, long-term cohort quality. Memory_31 and memory_91 provide corroborating evidence that onboarding simplification drives sustainable activation across self-serve and SMB segments. Promotional pricing is ruled out by exp_73's -12% retention damage despite short-term revenue gains—this conflicts with our primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Referral and activation messaging are secondary compared to fixing the onboarding funnel itself. Enterprise_sales_assist is viable but narrower in scope and does not address the observed activation/completion decline across our main user base. The onboarding experiment preserves uncertainty (we do not know if past results generalize to current competitive environment) while anchoring to the strongest evidence of durable, quality-preserving growth.
